origin.description: Raw, ratio, and regression estimates of the tail probability P(t <= t0) under importance resampling.
origin.usage: imp.prob(boot.out = NULL, index = 1, t0 = boot.out$t0[index], t = boot.out$t[, index], w = NULL, def = TRUE, q = NULL)

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A boot object from boot or tilt.boot. Required when t, t0, or the importance weights are not supplied.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: Column of the statistic to use when t or t0 is not supplied. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Points at which the bootstrap distribution function is estimated. The default is the observed value of the selected statistic.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates of the statistic. The default is the selected column of boot.out$t.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Importance weights, one per replicate. If omitted, they are computed by imp.weights.

arguments.name: def
arguments.text: Passed to imp.weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Target resampling probabilities, passed to imp.weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

origin.details: Non-finite replicates are dropped, along with their weights. The raw estimate is the sum of the weights on replicates at most t0, divided by the number of replicates, and is capped at 1. The ratio estimate is the largest value of cumsum(w)/sum(w) at a replicate at most t0. The regression estimate is the same cumulative probability after the weights are replaced by the regression weights from imp.reg. If no replicate is at most t0, the ratio and regression estimates are 0.
origin.value: A list with components t0, raw, rat, and reg. raw, rat, and reg each have one estimate per value of t0.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(boot))
set.seed(1)
x <- c(10, 12, 9, 15, 11, 14)
weights <- c(0.05, 0.15, 0.1, 0.3, 0.25, 0.15)
statistic <- function(d, w) sum(d * w) / sum(w)
b <- boot(x, statistic, R = 12, stype = "w", weights = weights)
print(imp.prob(b))

translation.description: Raw, ratio, and regression estimates of the tail probability P(t <= t0) under importance resampling.
translation.usage: imp_prob(boot_out=None, index=1, t0=None, t=None, w=None, def_=True, q=None)

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: Bootstrap object with t, t0, data, weights, strata, R, and frequency. Required when t, t0, or the importance weights are omitted. frequency is the resample count matrix copied from boot.array.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based column of the statistic to use when t or t0 is omitted. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Points at which the bootstrap distribution function is estimated. Omitted means the observed value boot_out.t0 at index.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates of the statistic. Omitted means the selected column of boot_out.t.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Importance weights, one per replicate. Omitted means they are computed by imp_weights.

arguments.name: def_
arguments.text: This is def in R. Passed to imp_weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Target resampling probabilities, passed to imp_weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

translation.details: Non-finite replicates are dropped, along with their weights. The raw estimate is the sum of the weights on replicates at most t0, divided by the number of replicates, and is capped at 1. The ratio estimate is the largest value of cumsum(w)/sum(w) at a replicate at most t0. The regression estimate is the same cumulative probability after the weights are replaced by the regression weights. If no replicate is at most t0, the ratio and regression estimates are 0.
translation.value: A dict with keys t0, raw, rat, and reg. raw, rat, and reg each have one estimate per value of t0.
